mainTopic: Which doorways need a מזוזה, where and on what it is written, and the rule that every letter of תפילין counts
overview: The amud finishes the discussion of a gatehouse and rules, following רב and שמואל, that it gets a מזוזה. רב הונא and רב פפא teach that every entrance needs its own מזוזה, even the doors people rarely use. אמימר adds that a doorway at a corner counts, because the ends of the walls serve as its doorposts. A story about מר שמואל's one-post doorway leads the גמרא to the sources for two rules. The first is that a מזוזה goes on the right side. The second is the dispute between רבי מאיר and the חכמים about a doorway with only one doorpost. A ברייתא then teaches, through a גזירה שוה, that a מזוזה is written on parchment with ink, not on stone. Finally, the גמרא explains the משנה's rule that even one letter invalidates תפילין. It ties this to רב's rule that every letter must be surrounded by blank parchment.

steps.title: The gatehouse is built for the garden
steps.stepSummary: This closes the explanation of רבה and רב יוסף: in the view of the רבנן, the gatehouse is built for the sake of the garden, so it is exempt from מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is made for the purpose of the garden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reason רבה and רב יוסף gave for the רבנן: the gatehouse serves the garden, not the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזוזה is needed on a doorway that serves a home where people live. If the gatehouse exists only to reach the garden, it does not count as part of the house. So even its inner entrance does not need a מזוזה according to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: With the intention of; for the purpose of
Gatehouse: the entry area discussed just before this

phrases.english: It is made for the purpose of the garden.
phrases.notes: "It" is the gatehouse from the discussion right before this line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the רבנן's view that was begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, a gatehouse is built to serve the garden, so it is exempt from מזוזה.

steps.title: How the אמוראים acted in practice
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא followed רבה and רב יוסף. רב אשי followed רב and שמואל, who are stringent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא acted like רבה and רב יוסף, and רב אשי acted like רב and שמואל, to be stringent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how different אמוראים actually behaved about the gatehouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two explanations of the earlier dispute. Following רבה and רב יוסף means no מזוזה on the gatehouse entrances. Following רב and שמואל means putting up a מזוזה, the stricter practice.

keyTerms.meaning: They acted; this was their practice

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava would act
in accordance with Rabba and Rav Yosef,
and Rav Ashi would act
in accordance with Rav and Shmuel, stringently,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא עָבְדִי כְּרַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reasoning to how sages actually acted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different אמוראים acted according to different explanations.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב and שמואל, stringently
steps.stepSummary: The final ruling: the הלכה follows רב and שמואל, who are stringent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רב and שמואל, stringently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the gatehouse question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though great אמוראים acted the other way, the הלכה is to be stringent. This means placing a מזוזה on the gatehouse entrances.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha; the final practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: For a gatehouse, the הלכה follows רב and שמואל: be stringent and put up a מזוזה.

phrases.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Rav and Shmuel, stringently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two practices reported in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב and שמואל: a מזוזה is required, to be stringent.

steps.title: An opening between a house and the upper floor
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a לול needs one מזוזה if it has one entrance and two if it has two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: about a לול opening from the house to the upper floor, רב הונא said: if it has one entrance, it needs one מזוזה. If it has two entrances, it needs two מזוזות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא counts מזוזות by counting entrances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is simple: each entrance is its own doorway, and each doorway needs its own מזוזה. A לול with an entrance both below and above gets two.

keyTerms.meaning: An opening or passage leading up to an upper floor

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר: לוּל פָּתוּחַ מִן הַבַּיִת לַעֲלִיָּיה,
phrases.english: It was stated: An aperture that opens from a house to a loft,
Rav Huna says:
If it has one entrance –
it is obligated in one mezuza;
if it has two entrances –
phrases.notes: One entrance from below and one from above.

phrases.english: it is obligated in two mezuzot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: לוּל פָּתוּחַ מִן הַבַּיִת לַעֲלִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about counting entrances.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each entrance of a לול needs its own מזוזה.

steps.title: A room with four doors needs four מזוזות
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from רב הונא that a room with four doors needs four מזוזות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: learn from רב הונא that a room with four doors needs four מזוזות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes רב הונא's rule and applies it to a room with four doors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every entrance counts on its own, then a room with four doors needs four מזוזות, not just one. This step sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Learn from that statement of Rav Huna

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אִינְדְּרוֹנָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ אַרְבְּעָה בָּאבֵי –
phrases.english: that this room which has four gates –
is obligated in four mezuzot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from רב הונא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A room with four doors needs four מזוזות.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say something so obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: once רב הונא counts each entrance, four doors needing four מזוזות seems to need no teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no statement is said without a reason. If it already follows from רב הונא, what new point is רב פפא adding?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether step 5 adds anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to follow directly from רב הונא, so there should be no need to say it.

steps.title: Even if only one door is usually used
steps.stepSummary: The new point is that all four doors need a מזוזה even though people usually use only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for the case where people usually use just one door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב פפא added: all four doors need a מזוזה even when only one is in regular use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think only the door people actually use counts. רב פפא teaches that every doorway counts, even the ones used less.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case

steps.whatToRemember: Every doorway needs a מזוזה, even if people usually walk through only one of them.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
even though one is accustomed to using one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, אַף עַל גַּב דִּרְגִיל בְּחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a less obvious case where the rule still applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps only the door people regularly use needs a מזוזה.
steps.terutzMaskana: All four doors need a מזוזה, even when only one is used regularly.

steps.title: A doorway at the corner needs a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that a doorway set at the corner of a house needs a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: a doorway at the corner needs a מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: אמימר says a corner doorway is obligated in מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A corner doorway is unusual because it is not set into the middle of a wall. Even so, אמימר rules that it counts as a doorway, which sets up רב אשי's challenge.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
This entrance which is at the corner
is obligated in a mezuza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about which openings count as doorways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doorway at a corner needs a מזוזה.

steps.title: But it has no doorposts
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects that a corner doorway has no doorposts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: but it has no doorposts!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר: a מזוזה goes on a doorpost, and this doorway seems not to have any.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doorway normally has doorposts on its sides. At a corner, the opening seems to lack them, so where would a מזוזה even go?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But it does not have doorposts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that a corner doorway needs a מזוזה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מזוזה requires doorposts, and a corner doorway seems to have none.

steps.title: These are its doorposts
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the ends of the walls count as the doorposts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: these are its doorposts.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers that the doorway does have doorposts: the edges of the walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doorpost does not need to be a separate post. The wall edges on each side of the opening do the same job, so the corner doorway needs a מזוזה.
steps.whatToRemember: A corner doorway needs a מזוזה, because the ends of the walls count as its doorposts.

phrases.english: He said to him: These are its doorposts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's objection in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what counts as a doorpost
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A corner doorway has no doorposts, so it is exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ends of the walls serve as doorposts, so a מזוזה is required.

steps.title: רב פפא sees a מזוזה on a one-post doorway
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא visits מר שמואל and sees a doorway with only one doorpost, on the left, that has a מזוזה on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא came to the house of מר שמואל. He saw a doorway that had only one doorpost, on the left side, and a מזוזה had been put on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to set up a question. This step only describes what רב פפא saw; his challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details matter here. The doorway has just one doorpost, and that post is on the left side. Both details will raise questions about whether a מזוזה belongs there.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa happened to come to the house of Mar Shmuel,
he saw a certain doorway
that had nothing but
one doorpost, on the left,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the Hebrew words in round brackets; the Aramaic words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Both mean 'one doorpost.'

phrases.english: and a mezuzah had been put on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about a doorway with only one doorpost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר שמואל put a מזוזה on a doorway with a single doorpost on the left.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר may only mean a right-side post
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whose view מר שמואל followed. רבי מאיר requires a מזוזה with one post, but perhaps only when that post is on the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Whose opinion are you following? רבי מאיר's? You could say רבי מאיר only said this when the one post is on the right. Did he say it about a post on the left?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges מר שמואל's practice. Even the most lenient view may not cover a single post on the left side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a doorway with only one doorpost still needs a מזוזה. But a מזוזה belongs on the right side, so maybe רבי מאיר only meant a case where the single post is on the right. Here the post is on the left, so even רבי מאיר might not require a מזוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose opinion are you following?

phrases.english: He said to him: According to whom?
According to Rabbi Meir?
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר requires a מזוזה even when there is only one doorpost. The גמרא brings his source in a few steps.

phrases.english: One could say Rabbi Meir only said it when the post is on the right;
did he say it about a post on the left?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר שמואל's placing a מזוזה on a single left-side doorpost.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even רבי מאיר, who requires a מזוזה with one post, may only mean a post on the right, since a מזוזה belongs on the right side.

steps.title: What is the source for the right side?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the מזוזה goes on the right side.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source for this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a background question. It wants to know where the rule comes from that a מזוזה goes on the right, the rule רב פפא just relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's challenge assumed that a מזוזה belongs on the right side. Before going further, the גמרא wants the source for that assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What is the source for this?

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: He means: where do we learn that the מזוזה goes on the right side?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the right-side rule assumed in the challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a מזוזה must be placed on the right side.

steps.title: Your house means your entering, from the right
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the word ביתך as ביאתך, the way you enter, and concludes that the מזוזה goes on the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: 'Your house' (ביתך) should be read as 'your entering' (ביאתך), which means the right side. You might ask: is it the right, or maybe the left? The פסוק says 'your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It ties the right-side rule to the word ביתך in the פסוק of מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא plays on the similar sound of ביתך (your house) and ביאתך (your entering). The מזוזה goes on the side that matches how you enter, and the ברייתא says that is the right. How the word ביתך proves 'right' is still not clear, so the גמרא asks about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Your house (from the פסוק of מזוזה)
Your entering, the way you come in
The פסוק teaches, therefore the פסוק says

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'your house' means 'your entering,'
phrases.notes: דברים 6:9

phrases.english: which is from the right.
You say it is from the right,
or perhaps it is really from the left?
The verse says: 'your house.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ביתך is read as ביאתך: the מזוזה goes on the side you enter by, which is the right.

steps.title: How does that word prove the right side?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the word ביתך shows that the מזוזה goes on the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the proof here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא's proof works. The word 'your house' does not obviously mean 'right.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא answered 'is it left?' just by repeating ביתך. That does not explain why 'entering' means the right side. The גמרא wants that missing link.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the learning? How does this proof work?

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the ברייתא's proof works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How ביתך / ביאתך shows that the side is the right.

steps.title: People step in with the right foot first
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that people start walking with the right foot, so 'the way you enter' is from the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The way you enter is from the right, because when a person lifts his foot to walk, he lifts his right foot first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה fills in the missing link in the ברייתא's proof, using how people naturally walk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Your entering' points to how a person enters. People naturally begin walking with the right foot, so entering is 'from the right.' That is why the מזוזה goes on the right side of the doorway.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifts his foot to start walking

steps.whatToRemember: A מזוזה goes on the right side of the doorway. ביתך is read as ביאתך, and people enter by stepping first with the right foot.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: דֶּרֶךְ בִּיאָתְךָ מִן הַיָּמִין,
phrases.english: Rabbah said: The way you enter is from the right,
because when a person lifts his foot,
he lifts the right one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: דֶּרֶךְ בִּיאָתְךָ מִן הַיָּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about how the proof works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People step first with the right foot, so entering is from the right.

steps.title: A second source: יהוידע's chest on the right
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אחא brings another source for the right side: יהוידע placed the charity chest on the right of the people entering the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אחא said before רב פפא, in the name of רבא בר עולא: We learn it from here: 'And יהוידע the כהן took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the מזבח, on the right as a person comes into the house of ה'. And the כהנים who guarded the threshold put there all the money brought into the house of ה'.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different source for the right-side rule, a פסוק from נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chest was placed "on the right as a person comes into the house of ה׳." This shows that something set up for people entering goes on their right. The same applies to a מזוזה.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Acha, before Rav Pappa,

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: said in the name of Rava bar Ulla: We learn it from here:
'And Yehoyada the priest took a chest,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 12:10

phrases.english: and bored a hole in its lid,
and placed it beside the altar,
on the right as a person comes into the House of ה׳;
and the priests who guarded the threshold put in there

phrases.aramaic: אֶת כׇּל הַכֶּסֶף הַמּוּבָא בֵית ה׳״.
phrases.english: all the money that was brought into the House of ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the right-side rule in place of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a מזוזה goes on the right side of the entrance.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 12:10: יהוידע's chest was placed 'on the right as a person comes in.'

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי מאיר's view that רב פפא mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the teaching of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב פפא's challenge. It asks where רבי מאיר's opinion about a one-post doorway is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא mentioned רבי מאיר without quoting him. Now the גמרא brings the actual teaching so we can see what he said.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the teaching of רבי מאיר referred to?

phrases.english: What is the teaching of Rabbi Meir?
phrases.notes: He means the opinion of רבי מאיר that רב פפא mentioned back in step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the right-side discussion to רבי מאיר's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי מאיר's opinion on a doorway with one doorpost.

steps.title: רבי מאיר obligates, the חכמים exempt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a house with only one doorpost needs a מזוזה according to רבי מאיר, while the חכמים say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: A house with only one doorpost: רבי מאיר says it needs a מזוזה, and the חכמים say it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא where רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about a one-post doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source of רבי מאיר's view. He requires a מזוזה even with one doorpost, while the חכמים exempt it. The ברייתא does not say which side the post is on, which is why רב פפא could suggest that רבי מאיר means only the right side.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: בַּיִת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא פַּצִּים אֶחָד,
phrases.english: As it is taught: A house that has only one doorpost:
Rabbi Meir requires a mezuzah,
and the Sages exempt it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: בַּיִת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא פַּצִּים אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר requires a מזוזה for a one-post doorway, and the חכמים exempt it.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים say a one-post doorway does not need a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exempting a doorway from מזוזה needs a reason. The גמרא looks for it in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (here, the חכמים of the ברייתא)

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the חכמים's exemption.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים exempt a doorway with only one doorpost.

steps.title: The Torah says doorposts, plural
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים's reason is that the תורה writes מזוזות, in the plural, so a doorway needs two doorposts.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'doorposts' (מזוזות).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים learn from the plural word מזוזות in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to write on the 'doorposts' of your house, in the plural. That suggests a doorway needs at least two posts to require a מזוזה. With only one post, the חכמים say there is no obligation.
steps.whatToRemember: A doorway with one doorpost: רבי מאיר requires a מזוזה, and the חכמים exempt it because the פסוק says מזוזות, in the plural, which means two posts.

phrases.english: 'Doorposts' is written.
phrases.notes: דברים 6:9. The plural word tells the חכמים you need two doorposts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the חכמים's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural מזוזות means a doorway needs two doorposts to require a מזוזה.

steps.title: What is the reason for רבי מאיר's view?
steps.stepSummary: Having explained the חכמים, the גמרא now asks for the reason of רבי מאיר, who says one doorpost is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר says that a doorway with only one doorpost still needs a מזוזה. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים learned from the plural word מזוזות that two doorposts are needed. So רבי מאיר must explain how he reads that same plural word to mean that one doorpost is enough.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels Step 20. That step asked for the חכמים's reason, and this one asks for רבי מאיר's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for requiring a מזוזה even when there is only one doorpost.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: two plurals limit the count to one doorpost
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי ישמעאל. The first 'מזוזות' would mean two, but the second 'מזוזות' is an extra inclusion, and an inclusion after an inclusion comes to limit. So one doorpost is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'doorposts' alone would tell me the smallest number is two. But the תורה says 'doorposts' again in the second פרשה, which it did not need to say. That makes an inclusion after an inclusion, and such a pair only comes to limit. So the פסוק limits it down to one doorpost. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that gives רבי ישמעאל's derivation. Since the תורה writes 'מזוזות' twice, the second one cuts the requirement down to one doorpost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plural normally means at least two. However, there is a rule that when the תורה adds a second inclusion on top of a first one, the pair works to limit instead of to expand. This is the source for רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The minimum meaning of the plural 'doorposts' is two
The second פרשה of קריאת שמע (והיה אם שמוע)
The פסוק did not need to say this, so it must be teaching something

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that two inclusions would limit, but that is the rule here: רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי אֶלָּא לְמַעֵט. The second plural does not add more doorposts. It brings the count down to one.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "doorposts"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:9

phrases.english: I would understand that the minimum of "doorposts" is two
when it says "doorposts" in the second passage,
phrases.notes: דברים 11:20

phrases.english: which the verse had no need to say,
it is an inclusion following an inclusion,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי אֶלָּא לְמַעֵט,
phrases.english: and an inclusion following an inclusion comes only to limit,
so the verse limited it to one doorpost.
These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מְזוּזוֹת שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי מִיעוּט מְזוּזוֹת שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repeated word 'מזוזות' is a רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי, which limits the requirement to one doorpost.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the extra word 'two' sets a pattern
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gets the same result differently. The פסוק in מצרים says 'the two doorposts', and the word 'two' is extra. This teaches that a plain 'מזוזות' means only one, unless the תורה spells out two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says this proof is not needed. The פסוק says 'on the lintel and on the two doorposts', and there was no need to write 'two'. So why does it say 'two'? It sets up a general rule: wherever it says 'doorposts', it means only one, unless the פסוק spells out two for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי עקיבא. He gives a different proof that one doorpost is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'מזוזות' already meant two, the word 'שתי' in שמות would be pointless. Its presence shows that the plain word 'מזוזות' means one. This becomes a בָּנָה אָב, a general pattern for every place the word appears.

keyTerms.meaning: This proof is not needed; there is a simpler source
The lintel, the beam across the top of a doorway
Set up a general pattern that applies everywhere

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא support רבי מאיר: a plain 'מזוזות' can mean just one doorpost. They only differ in how they prove it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: This is not needed,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״עַל הַמַּשְׁקוֹף וְעַל שְׁתֵּי הַמְּזוּזֹת״,
phrases.english: since when it says: "on the lintel and on the two doorposts,"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:22, the blood placed on the doorways in מצרים.

phrases.english: there was no need for the verse to say "two".
Why does the verse say "two"?
This set up a general pattern:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״מְזוּזוֹת״ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אַחַת,
phrases.english: anywhere it says "doorposts," it means only one,
unless the verse spells out two for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different derivation for the same conclusion as Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'שתי' in שמות 12:22 shows that a plain 'מזוזות' means one doorpost.

steps.title: A מזוזה is written on a ספר, learned from another 'writing'
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא asks whether a מזוזה could be written on the stones of the doorway. It answers by comparing the word 'writing' here to a 'writing' elsewhere that is done on a ספר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And you shall write them.' I might think one writes it on the stones. The word 'writing' is said here, and 'writing' is said there. Just as there it is on a ספר, so too here it is on a ספר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what material a מזוזה is written on. The ברייתא suggests the stones of the doorway, then rejects that by comparing two uses of the word 'writing'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same word, כתיבה, in two places to learn one from the other. Since that other writing is done on a ספר, a מזוזה must also be written on a ספר, meaning parchment, and not on the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: It is said here and it is said there; learning one case from another through a shared word
A scroll or book, meaning parchment

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "And you shall write them"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:9

phrases.english: I might think one writes it on the stones?
phrases.notes: He means the stones of the doorway itself.

phrases.english: "Writing" is said here,
and "writing" is said there.
Just as there it is on a book,
so too here it is on a book.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וּכְתַבְתָּם יָכוֹל יִכְתְּבֶנָּה עַל הָאֲבָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the writing surface of a מזוזה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזוזה is written on a ספר (parchment), learned from another כתיבה that is done on a ספר.

steps.title: Maybe compare it to the writing on stones instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back on itself. Maybe the comparison should be to the writing on the stones, and then a מזוזה would be written on stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: 'writing' is said here, and 'writing' is said there. Just as there it is on the stones, so too here it is on the stones!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own comparison. There is another 'writing' in the תורה that is done on stones, so maybe a מזוזה should follow that one. This sets up the next move, which must explain which comparison is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same method, matching the word כתיבה, can point in two directions: to a ספר or to stones. Until the ברייתא shows why one comparison is better, the proof in Step 25 is not settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this other way; a challenge offering a competing comparison

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the conclusion. The ברייתא is only raising a competing option. The next step decides between the ספר and the stones.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
"Writing" is said here,
and "writing" is said there,
phrases.notes: This 'there' is the writing on the stones when entering ארץ ישראל (דברים 27:3).

phrases.english: just as there it is on the stones,
so too here it should be on the stones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison made in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the מזוזה's כתיבה to a כתיבה done on a ספר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word כתיבה also appears where the writing is on stones. Without a reason to prefer the ספר, the comparison could just as well require writing on stones.

steps.title: A מזוזה is compared to a ספר, not to the stones, and is written with ink
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא decides that a מזוזה is learned from the writing of a ספר, because both are for all generations. The stones writing was not. It also learns from ירמיהו that a ספר is written with ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which comparison fits better. We learn a writing that is done in every generation from another writing that is done in every generation. We do not learn it from a writing that is not done in every generation. And as it says there: 'And ברוך said to them: He read all these words to me from his mouth, and I write them on the scroll with ink.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question from the last step. It picks the comparison to a ספר, not to the stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזוזה is a מצוה for all time, just like writing a ספר. The writing on the stones was only done once, so it is a weaker match. The פסוק from ירמיהו adds that this kind of ספר writing is done with ink.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which it is more similar to
We derive, we learn one case from another
Applies in all generations, a lasting מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that a מזוזה is written on a scroll and with ink.

phrases.english: Let us see which it resembles.
We derive a writing that applies in all generations
from a writing that applies in all generations,
and we do not derive a writing that applies in all generations
from a writing that does not apply in all generations.
And as it is stated elsewhere:
"And Baruch said to them: From his mouth
he would call out to me all these words,
and I write them on the scroll with ink."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 36:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the ברייתא's own challenge from step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picking the better of two possible comparisons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe a מזוזה is compared to the writing on the stones
steps.terutzMaskana: It is compared to a ספר, since both are for all generations, and it is written with ink

steps.title: Why use a comparison when the פסוק says 'on the doorposts'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges רב אשי: the פסוק says to write on the doorposts, so why learn from a גזירה שוה that it goes on a scroll?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: The תורה says 'on the doorposts', and you say we should learn 'writing' from 'writing'?
steps.whatsHappening: A later אמורא attacks the comparison. He says the plain words of the פסוק point to writing right on the doorpost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וכתבתם על מזוזות' sounds like you write directly on the doorpost itself. So how can a comparison override the simple meaning and move the writing to a scroll?

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
'Writing' and 'writing', the shared word used for the comparison

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
The Merciful One says "on the doorposts,"
and you say: let us learn "writing" from "writing"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison used in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה that a מזוזה is written on a scroll
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain wording 'on the doorposts' seems to mean writing directly on the doorpost

steps.title: First a complete writing, then onto the doorposts
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that 'וכתבתם' hints at 'כתיבה תמה', a complete writing, which is done first and only then placed on the doorposts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'וכתבתם', meaning a complete writing, and only afterward 'on the doorposts'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that the פסוק itself does not mean writing on the doorpost. You write first, then put it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'וכתבתם' as 'כתיבה תמה', a finished writing. So the words 'on the doorposts' tell you where to place it after writing, not where to write.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And you shall write them,"
meaning a complete writing,
phrases.notes: A wordplay: וּכְתַבְתָּם sounds like כְּתִיבָה תַּמָּה.

phrases.english: and only then "on the doorposts."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מזוזה is written directly on the doorpost
steps.terutzMaskana: It is written completely first, and then placed on the doorpost

steps.title: Then why is the comparison needed at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if 'וכתבתם' already teaches that we write first and then attach, why do we need the גזירה שוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is written 'וכתבתם', why do I need this גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the comparison from the other side. If the פסוק already teaches it, the comparison looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's answer seems to make the גזירה שוה unnecessary. The גמרא asks what extra thing the comparison still teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison between two places in the Torah that use the same word

phrases.english: And since it is written "And you shall write them,"
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; the corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: why do I need this גזירה שוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר דִּכְתִיב ״וּכְתַבְתָּם״, הַאי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 29 to question the need for step 27's comparison
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'וכתבתם' already teaches writing first and then attaching, the comparison seems extra

steps.title: Without the comparison, one might write on a stone
steps.stepSummary: Without the גזירה שוה, we might write the מזוזה on a stone and then attach the stone to the doorpost. The comparison teaches it must be on a ספר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the גזירה שוה, I would have said: let him write it on a stone and fix it to the doorpost. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each source teaches. 'וכתבתם' says write first; the comparison says write on a scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וכתבתם' only tells us to write before attaching, not what to write on. A stone would still fit that. The גזירה שוה to a ספר rules out the stone.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources work together: 'וכתבתם' teaches write first and then attach, and the גזירה שוה teaches it must be on a scroll, with ink.

phrases.english: If not for the גזירה שוה,
I would have said: let him write it on a stone
and fix it onto the doorpost.
So it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing each source teaches something different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Write the מזוזה on a stone and attach the stone to the doorpost
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה requires a scroll

steps.title: The משנה: the four פרשיות of תפילין hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the four פרשיות in the תפילין hold each other back, and even one missing letter holds them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The four passages in the תפילין hold each other back, and even one letter holds them back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about תפילין. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any one of the four פרשיות is missing, the מצוה is not done with the others. The same is true even if just one letter is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah passages written inside the תפילין
Each one holds back the others; without one, the others don't work

phrases.english: The four passages that are in the tefillin
hold each other back,
and even one letter holds them back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבַּע פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתְּפִילִּין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Missing any פרשה, or even one letter, ruins the תפילין

steps.title: Isn't this obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that even one letter holds them back. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for saying something that seems too obvious. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah says to write these פרשיות, of course every letter must be there. So the גמרא wants to know what new point the משנה is making.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the משנה's statement in step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words 'even one letter holds them back'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It goes without saying that a missing letter makes the writing incomplete

steps.title: The משנה teaches that even the tiny stroke of a י matters
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב answers that the משנה's 'even one letter' comes to teach that even the קוצו של יוד, the small stroke of a י, holds back the תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The משנה only needed to say this to teach about the small stroke of the letter י.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 33. The משנה's words come to teach that even the tiny stroke on a י, not only a whole missing letter, makes the תפילין not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole missing letter is obviously a problem. So רב reads the משנה as pointing to something smaller: if just the little stroke of the י is missing, the letter is still not properly formed, and the תפילין are held back.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'thorn' of a י: the tiny stroke that is part of the letter's shape
It was only needed for... (a formula that explains what a seemingly obvious teaching comes to add)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It was needed only
for the thorn of a yod.
phrases.notes: This is the tiny stroke at the edge of the letter י. Even if just that is missing, the letter isn't complete.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל יוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 33's question of why the משנה needs to mention one letter.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the teaching to a smaller case: a partial letter, not a whole missing letter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'one letter' seems to state the obvious point that a missing letter invalidates.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that even a missing stroke of a י invalidates.

steps.title: The tiny stroke of a י is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a missing קוץ of a י is also obviously a problem, so the משנה still would not need to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this too is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's answer. A י without its stroke is not a proper letter, so that is also obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is to find something the משנה teaches that we would not have known. If the letter's shape is broken, everyone would agree it is not valid, so the question from Step 33 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; no need to teach it

phrases.english: But this too is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 34's answer using the same 'obvious' question as Step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's answer that the משנה teaches about the קוצו של יוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A letter missing part of its shape is plainly not formed correctly, so it is just as obvious as a missing letter.

steps.title: Every letter must be surrounded by blank parchment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is needed for another rule of רב יהודה in the name of רב: any letter not surrounded by blank parchment on all four sides is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was only needed for the other teaching of רב יהודה. For רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Any letter that does not have blank parchment surrounding it on all four sides is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The משנה's 'even one letter' is needed for רב's rule that each letter must have blank parchment all around it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem is not a broken letter but a letter that touches something else, so its ink is not fully surrounded by clean parchment. This is not obvious, so the משנה needs to teach that even one such letter holds back the תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: Parchment; here, the blank part around a letter

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'even one letter holds them back' is explained through רב's rule of גויל מוקף: every letter must be surrounded by blank parchment on all four sides, or it is פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: This rule is not about a letter with a missing piece. The letter can look complete and still be פסול if its ink touches something on any side.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of גויל מוקף is a basic requirement for every letter in תפילין, מזוזות and ספרי תורה.

phrases.english: Rather, it was needed only
for the other teaching of Rav Yehuda,
as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Any letter that does not have parchment
